items.title: A man died. Why the laughing emoji?
items.summary: Have Malaysians become heartless? Fear becomes frustration. Frustration becomes anger.

items.title: September 'real battleground' for Indonesia in fight against forest fires as el Nino peaks
items.summary: JAKARTA: September will be Indonesia's "real battleground" in the fight against forest and land fires as El Nino reaches its peak, with the country still facing significant risks despite a decline in fire hotspots following a month of intensified firefighting efforts. "September is the peak of El Nino. Raja Juli said five measures would remain central to the government's efforts in September: weather modification operations (OMC), water bombing, ground firefighting, law enforcement and greater public awareness.

items.title: Rauf becomes delivery rider for a day
items.summary: MASJID TANAH: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh stepped into the shoes of a p-hailing rider, collecting food orders and delivering them to customers' homes to experience firsthand the daily routine of those working in the sector. Rauf said he appreciated the dedication of the riders, who work hard every day to support their families, and wanted to see for himself how they receive orders, collect food and make deliveries. "I tried to become one of the delivery riders and learn how they receive orders.

items.title: Father mulls legal action after son dies from suspected electrocution at futsal court
items.summary: Norramin Senin, 49, said that although he did not wish to blame any party, he hoped his son, Muhammad Anas Muazim, would be the last victim. Let my son be the only victim, and I hope no one else suffers the same fate," said the lorry driver. "But Allah loved him more," said Norramin.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - September 1, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Here are today's top stories. Arrested The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested a former minister in connection with issues arising from the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Temerloh crash A family's joyful trip home after attending the National Day celebrations in Putrajaya yesterday ended in tragedy when three family members were killed in an 11-vehicle crash at KM110.3 of the East Coast Expressway (LPT1) here last night.

items.title: Seni Jaya unit bags seven-year RTS Link advertising concession
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Seni Jaya Corp Bhd's unit SJX Media Sdn Bhd has clinched a seven-year advertising media concession for the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System Link (RTS Link). SJX Media entered into an advertising concession agreement with Malaysia Rapid Transit System Sdn Bhd (MRTS) on Sept 1 for the design, build, operation and transfer of advertising media facilities for the RTS Link. Under the agreement, SJX Media will have exclusive rights to design, procure, manufacture, install, test, commission, operate and maintain advertising media at designated spaces within the RTS Link.

items.title: MACC strengthens global cooperation against cross-border corruption
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has stepped up international cooperation in tackling cross-border corruption through its participation in the seventh plenary meeting of the Global Operational Network of Anti-Corruption Law Enforcement Authorities (GlobE Network). MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the platform enabled bilateral and multilateral discussions, the sharing of knowledge and developments, and cooperation on cross-border cases. Abd Halim said this was MACC's fourth participation since joining the network in May 2023, reflecting its continued commitment to international cooperation in cross-border corruption investigations, tracing illicit financial flows and asset recovery.

items.title: Ta Win unit to slash workforce by 52pct in cost-cutting move
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ta Win Holdings Bhd's subsidiary Ta Win Industries (M) Sdn Bhd will cut 39 jobs, or 52 per cent of its workforce, as part of a cost-cutting exercise. In a bourse filing, Ta Win said the exercise will begin on Sept 11 as it seeks to streamline operations, remove redundant positions and reduce costs amid current market conditions. However, Ta Win expects the job cuts to deliver longer-term cost savings and improve operational efficiency.

items.title: Pengerang investment must deliver measurable results, financial improvements, says industry expert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The multibillion-ringgit investment in Pengerang must now translate into measurable operational and financial improvements, particularly as PRefChem continues to face losses, said industry expert Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan. Commenting on a recent report on the financial performance of PRefChem, the chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd said the performance of the Pengerang Integrated Complex (PIC) should be assessed based on clear and transparent indicators rather than broad assurances. In statement, Jeyenderan said the benefits should extend beyond the financial performance of the complex, particularly in strengthening Malaysia’s domestic fuel security and diversifying crude sourcing.

items.title: From RM120 website to RM4mil in coffee sales
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A RM120 investment in a website helped local coffee entrepreneur Mirwan Badri Ahmad Badri turn a pandemic setback into nearly RM4 million in sales within two years. Mirwan Badri, 41, said his online marketplace, Buna Market, was launched in January 2020 to harness digital technology as Malaysia imposed movement restrictions during the Covid-19 pandemic. Within two years, our sales had almost reached RM4 million," he said.

items.title: Five-sen coin's future hangs in balance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Coins of various denominations have long been widely used in everyday transactions. Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said the use of five sen coins has declined, but there is still demand for them, particularly in the retail sector. "So, will there come a day when we no longer have 20 sen coins and only use 50 sen coins?

items.title: Malaysians urged to stay vigilant as Mount Sinabung erupts, flights disrupted, thousands evacuated
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 1 — Malaysians in or travelling to Karo Regency in North Sumatra have been advised to remain vigilant and avoid areas surrounding Mount Sinabung following its eruption on Monday, which disrupted flights and prompted the evacuation of more than 2,400 residents. In a statement on Tuesday, the Consulate General of Malaysia in Medan urged Malaysians to follow instructions issued by the Indonesian authorities, saying several flights at Medan’s Kualanamu International Airport, a key gateway to North Sumatra, had reportedly been rescheduled or cancelled due to volcanic ash. Following the eruption, Indonesia’s Geological Agency raised Mount Sinabung’s status from Level II (Alert) to Level III (Standby) at 12.30pm after visual and instrumental monitoring showed increased volcanic activity.

items.title: Forecast: Indonesian fire pollutants potentially moving towards Malaysia
items.summary: National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) Acting Head of Data, Information and Disaster Communication Centre Berton Panjaitan said Central Kalimantan recorded the highest number at 63, down from 72 a day earlier, while West Kalimantan fell to 30 from 104 and South Kalimantan to 13 from 55. "Visibility remained below 1km in West Kalimantan, about two kilometres in Central Kalimantan and below three kilometres in South Kalimantan," Berton said. Berton said ground teams had extinguished fires covering about 263ha in West Kalimantan, 87ha in Central Kalimantan and 29ha in South Kalimantan.

items.title: Alam Maritim to buy RM81mil OSV as subsea business expands
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Alam Maritim Resources Bhd plans to acquire a newly built offshore support vessel (OSV) for US$19.8 million (RM80.8 million) to expand its subsea operations and support its RM1.55 billion order book. The proposed acquisition will be undertaken through subsidiary Alam Maritim (M) Sdn Bhd (AMSB), which entered into a vessel purchase option agreement with Singapore-based Poet Shipbuilding & Engineering Pte Ltd on Dec 1, 2025. Under the agreement, AMSB paid an option fee of US$900,000 (RM3.67 million) for the right to purchase the vessel.

items.title: Kee Ming clinches RM40mil M&E jobs in Penang, Selangor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kee Ming Group Bhd's unit Kee Ming Electrical Sdn Bhd has secured two subcontracts worth a combined RM40 million for mechanical and electrical (M&E) engineering works at industrial projects in Penang and Selangor. The first subcontract, worth RM21 million, involves works for a warehouse in the Valdor Industrial Area, Penang. Kee Ming said the fixed-price, lump-sum contracts also include infrastructure works within the project boundaries, street lighting and card access systems, where applicable.

items.title: Global bond sell-off deepens on inflation concerns
items.summary: LONDON: A global bond sell-off deepened on Tuesday, pushing government borrowing costs higher and equities lower as investors worried that energy-driven inflation could force central banks to raise interest rates. Japan's 10-year government bond yield touched a 30-year high of three per cent, reflecting concerns over plans for massive government spending. The yield on the 30-year US Treasury bond stood at 5.27 per cent, not far from levels last seen in 2007, while the 10-year yield rose to its highest level since January 2025.

items.title: Malaysians advised to stay vigilant following Mount Sinabung eruption
items.summary: JAKARTA: Malaysians in or travelling to Karo Regency in North Sumatra have been advised to remain vigilant and avoid areas surrounding Mount Sinabung following its eruption on Monday, which disrupted flights and prompted the evacuation of more than 2,400 residents. In a statement on Tuesday, the Consulate General of Malaysia in Medan urged Malaysians to follow instructions issued by the Indonesian authorities, saying several flights at Medan's Kualanamu International Airport, a key gateway to North Sumatra, had reportedly been rescheduled or cancelled due to volcanic ash. Following the eruption, Indonesia's Geological Agency raised Mount Sinabung's status from Level II (Alert) to Level III (Standby) at 12.30pm after visual and instrumental monitoring showed increased volcanic activity.

items.title: Melaka to subsidise motorcycle servicing for over 3,000 p-hailing riders
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Melaka will introduce a motorcycle maintenance subsidy to ease the financial burden of over 3,000 p-hailing delivery riders across the state. Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the allocation will be tabled at the State Executive Council (Exco) meeting this week and announced next week. Ab Rauf said the initiative is part of the state government's efforts to appreciate p-hailing workers, who play a vital role in facilitating the community's daily affairs through digital platforms.

items.title: Former minister held by MACC to assist Tabung Haji RCI investigation on hotel deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) today detained a former minister to assist in investigations in connection with issues raised by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). According to a post on the MACC’s TikTok account, the arrest was linked to an issue involving a hotel lease agreement in Saudi Arabia. Meanwhile, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest when contacted, and said the case is being investigated under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Kuching man admits snatching mother’s gold necklace, judge jails him seven years
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 1 — A food delivery rider was sentenced on Tuesday to seven years’ jail and five strokes of the cane for snatching his own mother’s gold necklace. The accused also told police that he committed the act while under the influence of drugs. Background checks by police also showed he had several prior criminal records, including for drugs.

items.title: Visibility stays above minimum at Kuching Airport despite haze, only AirBorneo flights cancelled
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 1 — Operations at Kuching International Airport (KIA) remained largely unaffected despite worsening haze conditions, with only two flights cancelled as visibility in parts of Sarawak deteriorated. KIA senior manager Jun Iskandar Murshidi said the cancelled flights were the Kuching-Mukah and Kuching-Tanjung Manis services, both operated by AirBorneo Airways. “Selected flights are affected due to the worsening haze.

items.title: [UPDATED] Former minister arrested over Tabung Haji RCI probe
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested a former minister in connection with its probe into the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry's (RCI) report into Tabung Haji (TH). MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, confirmed the arrest. The MACC has made a slew of high-profile arrests over the TH RCI report's findings.

items.title: Pahang Sultan, Tengku Ampuan extend condolences to families of four killed in 11-vehicle crash
items.summary: According to a Pahang Sultanate Facebook post, Their Royal Highnesses expressed their sympathy to the victims' families during this difficult time following the tragedy. Meanwhile, Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail also expressed his condolences to the family of the three family members who were killed in the accident. Nazatul and Nur Atiqah Sofiya, both 32, and their four-year-old son Muhammad Armaan Nazeef were among four people killed in the accident .

items.title: MOH monitors rise in respiratory infections and conjunctivitis in Sarawak amid haze crisis
items.summary: SIBU, Sept 1 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is monitoring the increase in cases of acute respiratory tract infections (URTI) and conjunctivitis in Sarawak following the haze conditions affecting several areas in the state. Deputy Health Minister Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib said continuous monitoring is being carried out through health facilities including health clinics and hospitals to ensure that any increase in cases related to the haze can be dealt with immediately. She said based on monitoring by the Sarawak State Health Department (JKN), the average URTI cases increased from about 1,717 cases per week at the beginning of the year to 1,752 cases per week recently.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPT 1, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia bucked earlier gains, tracking weaker regional peers amid heightened geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran. The benchmark index fell 25.24 points to 1,700.54. In the crypto market, Bitcoin fell to RM314,936 Ethereum and Solana also slipped to RM9,891 and RM414, respectively.

items.title: Vstecs exits Isatec in RM48.75mil deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Vstecs Bhd is disposing of its entire 40 per cent stake in Isatec Sdn Bhd to Singapore-based Skyform Pte Ltd for RM48.75 million, nearly 2.6 times its original investment cost. Vstecs will receive RM48.75 million for its 233,334 shares, while the four management shareholders will collectively receive RM42.66 million for their 35 per cent stake. The company said the RM48.75 million consideration represents a 103.63 per cent premium over the RM23.94 million carrying value of its Isatec investment as at Dec 31, 2025, and a 159.31 per cent premium over its original investment cost of RM18.80 million.

items.title: Ringgit ends lower after US Fed hints at rate hike
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended lower against the greenback on the first trading day of September on rising expectations of a US interest rate hike after Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh's recent speech at the Jackson Hole Symposium. At 6pm, the ringgit fell to 4.0370/0410 against the US dollar from last Friday's close of 4.0230/0270. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Warsh's speech at the Jackson Hole Symposium last Friday has had a significant impact on the currencies market.

items.title: 'Hoping for a miracle': Hani refuses to give up on husband caught in Nepal floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: "I am still positive and hoping for a miracle," said Hani Othman, whose husband remains among the Malaysians uncontactable following the Nepal floods. Hani, who travelled to Kathmandu to seek updates on the search for her husband, senior fire officer Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, said she did not know how long she would remain in Nepal. She also asked the NGO to help search for her husband and his team in the affected area.

items.title: Serian tops API at 374, no monitoring station records 'good' air quality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Five monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 6pm today. 11 locations recorded "unhealthy" readings between 101 and 200, including four in Sarawak. Meanwhile, 48 locations recorded "moderate" API readings between 51 and 100.

items.title: Dunham-Bush invests RM172mil in Negri Sembilan expansion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Dunham-Bush Industries Sdn Bhd will invest approximately RM172 million in the first phase of a new manufacturing facility at SPD Tech Valley in Senawang, Negri Sembilan. The global manufacturer of heating, ventilation, air-conditioning and refrigeration (HVAC/R) solutions signed a sale and purchase agreement (SPA) with SPD Tech Valley Sdn Bhd for approximately 32 acres of industrial land at the industrial park. The SPA was signed by Dunham-Bush Industries Sdn Bhd managing director Yu Boashuang and Seri Pajam Development Group chief executive officer Ten Wee Seong, who represented SPD Tech Valley, at Park Hyatt, Kuala Lumpur on Aug 28.

items.title: Vulnerable groups urged to avoid outdoor activities as Sabah haze hits 4 areas
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) has advised vulnerable groups to avoid outdoor activities following unhealthy air quality recorded in several areas of the state. It said children, senior citizens, pregnant women and individuals with respiratory problems should also avoid strenuous and physically demanding activities. The public is also advised to ensure good ventilation indoors to reduce exposure to polluted air.

items.title: Reducing Indonesia wildfires will be challenging as El Nino peaks this month, minister warns
items.summary: JAKARTA: Efforts to reduce wildfires ablaze across Indonesia will be challenging as the El Nino weather phenomenon will peak this month, the forestry minister said on Tuesday, describing the devastation as largely man-made. Indonesia has intensified efforts to contain haze from forest and land fires across six provinces in Borneo and Sumatra islands. Hot spots were reduced across Kalimantan and Sumatra by the end of August, minister Raja Juli Antoni said.

items.title: Kuala Selangor police say teenager electrocuted after touching lamp post during futsal break
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 1 — A teenage boy died after being electrocuted while holding a lamp post in Taman Pancaran, Bestari Jaya, yesterday. Kuala Selangor police chief Supt Azaharudin Tajuddin said they received a call regarding the incident involving the 15-year-old boy at about 10.32pm. “The Kuala Selangor District Police Headquarters Operations Room received a call regarding a boy who was found unconscious and believed to be dead.

items.title: 262 motorcycles inspected, 155 summonses issued in Klang, Kuala Selangor operations
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A total of 262 motorcyclists were inspected, with 155 summonses issued for various traffic offences in two operations, codenamed Op Samseng Jalanan and Op Bersepadu Ambang Merdeka in Kuala Selangor and Klang respectively yesterday. The seven-hour operation resulted in the inspection of 140 vehicles, with 90 summonses issued for various traffic violations, in addition to the seizure of five motorcycles. Meanwhile, Klang South district police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said that in an operation on Persiaran Raja Muda Musa, Klang, a total of 122 motorcyclists were inspected and 65 traffic summonses were issued.

items.title: Haze: MOH monitoring URT, conjunctivitis cases
items.summary: SIBU: The Health Ministry (MOH) is monitoring the increase in cases of acute respiratory tract infections (URTI) and conjunctivitis in Sarawak following the haze conditions affecting several areas in the state. Deputy Health Minister Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib said continuous monitoring is being carried out through health facilities including health clinics and hospitals to ensure that any increase in cases related to the haze can be dealt with immediately. She said based on monitoring by the Sarawak State Health Department, the average URTI cases increased from about 1,717 cases per week at the beginning of the year to 1,752 cases per week recently.

items.title: India busts firm faking expiry dates, nutrition labels on PepsiCo, Nestle food exports
items.summary: MUMBAI: Indian authorities have raided an illegal operation in Mumbai that faked expiry dates and nutritional information on original food products manufactured by PepsiCo, Nestle, Coca-Cola and Unilever so they could be exported to other countries. Reuters got exclusive access to the warehouse last week as food officers conducted a six-day investigation and seized goods worth nearly US$80,000. A photographer saw chemicals used to remove manufacturers' original expiry dates and ingredient labels, machines to print and apply replacements and scores of label packs for products including Lay's potato chips and Maggi noodles.

items.title: Agrobank to fully disburse RM200mil under oil palm smallholder scheme by October
items.summary: SERDANG: Bank Pertanian Malaysia Bhd (Agrobank) aims to fully utilise RM200 million in financing for oil palm smallholders under the TSPKS 2.0 replanting scheme by October this year. Agrobank has so far approved 4,380 applications worth RM190.99 million, group president and group chief executive officer Datuk Tengku Ahmad Badli Shah Raja Hussin said. "We are targeting RM200 million to be fully financed by October this year," he said after the launch of the Smallholder Oil Palm Replanting Financing Incentive Scheme (TSPKS) 2.0 system today.

items.title: ‘Literally tasting the smoke’: Sarawakians suffer as haze worsens
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 1 — Air quality in Malaysia's Sarawak state deteriorated further today as smoke from Indonesian forest fires drove up respiratory complaints and sent residents scrambling for protective masks. Six districts in Sarawak, on Borneo, recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, including the state capital, Kuching, where the API hit 407. Mason said the worsening air had also affected her health, causing a sore throat and aggravating her asthma.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji chairman, ex-Treasury sec-gen released from MACC custody in RCI-linked probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — A former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman and a former Treasury secretary-general were reportedly released from Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) custody today in an investigation linked to a royal commission of inquiry (RCI) report on the pilgrims’ fund. The politician and former TH chairman and the former Finance Ministry official were arrested at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya on August 26. Before that, MACC detained seven people comprising a shipping company chief executive officer, two company directors and four former members of TH’s senior management.

items.title: Ayer Itam brawl involved Geng 04 members in debt dispute, Penang police say
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 1 — Police have confirmed that an armed fight that caused two individuals to suffer severe injuries in front of a National Type Chinese Primary School in Ayer Itam here on Saturday involved Geng 04 members. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said all 13 men arrested to facilitate investigations into the case are believed to be members of the same gang but in different areas and the fight was due to a misunderstanding over debts. He said the two severely injured men, in their 30s, were not gang members but were attacked when they were misidentified as suspects involved in the fight, adding the victims were on their way back from a religious festival when they were attacked by the group.

items.title: Three-year-old boy found dead below Victoria Bridge in Kuala Kangsar
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR, Sept 1 — A three-year-old boy was reportedly found dead on a road beneath the Victoria Bridge in Enggor here yesterday evening. Sinar Harian reported that Abdul Rafee Abdul Halim was taken to Kuala Kangsar Hospital, where he was pronounced dead at about 7.40pm. The Kuala Kangsar Municipal Council subsequently cordoned off the bridge with safety tape.

items.title: Penang police arrest married couple, two others in drug syndicate on Thai intel tip
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 1 — Police have arrested four members of an international drug syndicate, including a married couple, and seized 86 kilogrammes of methamphetamine worth RM4.31 million in a series of raids in Selangor and Penang recently. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the success was the result of intelligence sharing between the Royal Malaysia Police and the Royal Thai Police after Thai authorities arrested a Malaysian man in Hua Hin, Thailand, on Aug 8. Thai narcotics police conducted an investigation and obtained intelligence, which was subsequently shared with the Malaysian Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID).

items.title: Duta Enclave: Court told RM1.39m payout to Semantan Estate was more than adequate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, September 1 — The High Court was told today that the RM1.39 million in compensation paid by the Government of Malaysia to Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition of 263.272 acres of land, known as the Duta Enclave, in 1956 was more than adequate. “I have prepared an expert valuation report to determine adequate compensation, in accordance with the Court of Appeal Order dated June 24, 2025, which, among others, fixed the valuation date for determining compensation for the said land as December 3, 1956. “Given that the government had previously paid compensation of $1,390,602.70 (in 1956) to the plaintiff (Semantan Estate), that amount exceeds the compensation I recommended under Valuation Basis 1.

items.title: Former PM Muhyiddin, ‘Azman’ and ‘Adam’ listed in same July 2020 golf game at Tropicana, witness tells court
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin played in a golf game in July 2020 at Tropicana Golf Club with 14 other players, including two individuals identified as “Azman” and “Adam”, Tropicana Golf & Country Resort Berhad (TGCRB) employee Saravanan Subaramaniam told the High Court today. TGCRB group head of security Saravanan said this while testifying as the 28th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s power abuse and money laundering trial. Saravanan said Tropicana Golf Club’s digital golf registration system showed that Muhyiddin and the 14 other individuals had played there in four “flights”, or groups, on July 19, 2020, with a single invoice issued for all 15 players.

items.title: Juwai IQI: Malaysia among top destinations for Chinese property buyers, investment on track to top RM1.6b a year
items.summary: According to new insights released today by Juwai IQI, the profile of Chinese buyers in Malaysia is undergoing a significant transformation. “Malaysia is now the fourth most popular destination for Chinese property buyers, up from sixth in 2025 and from seventh in 2022, 2023, and 2024,” Kashif said. In 2024, Malaysia attracted 2.8 per cent of global property enquiries from Chinese homebuyers, with the figure climbing to 4.5 per cent in 2025.

items.title: Perak assembly to choose new senator between PKR and PAS nominees
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 1 — The upcoming Perak State Legislative Assembly sitting will see a motion tabled to elect a new senator, Speaker Datuk Seri Mohammad Zahir Abdul Khalid said. Mohammad Zahir said the motion would be tabled by Mentri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad. He also said two Bills would be tabled during the sitting, namely the Administrative Members and State Assembly Members (Salary) Enactment 2026 and the Islamic Religious Administration (Perak) (Amendment) Enactment 2026.

items.title: Deadly LPT1 pile-up: Four dead include family returning from National Day parade in Putrajaya
items.summary: Mohd Kazwan Mohd Kassim, 59, the father of one of the victims, Nur Atiqah Sofiya, 32, said it was the first time his daughter, her husband, Muhammad Nazatul Nazmi, 32, and their son, Muhammad Armaan Nazeef, four, had celebrated National Day in Putrajaya. Meanwhile, the victim’s cousin, Nur Awatif Adawiyah Abdul Aziz, 30, said Nur Atiqah Sofiya had sent photos of the National Day celebrations to the family’s WhatsApp group and also uploaded photos to her Instagram Story. We never thought these photos would become their last memories,” she said.

items.title: Court of Appeal allows Rosmah to introduce new evidence in solar graft appeal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Court of Appeal today allowed applications by former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s wife, Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her corruption conviction, paving the way for the evidence to be heard by the High Court. A three-member panel comprising Justices Choo Kah Sing, Azhahari Kamal Ramli and K. Muniandy allowed both applications before it and ordered that the additional evidence be taken before another High Court judge. Justice Choo, who read the panel’s decision, said the court was satisfied that the requirements for admitting the additional evidence had been met.

items.title: Sabah disaster committee urges public to limit outdoor activities as four districts record unhealthy API
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 1 — The Sabah State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) has urged the public, particularly vulnerable groups, to limit outdoor activities and avoid strenuous physical exertion after four locations across the state recorded unhealthy air pollutant index (API) levels today. The committee issued the advisory as hazy conditions shrouded several districts, calling on children, senior citizens, pregnant women, and individuals suffering from respiratory illnesses to exercise extra caution. The advisory comes as data from the Sabah Department of Environment (DOE) showed air quality worsening across multiple monitoring stations as of 8am today.

items.title: Islamic affairs minister denounces Malaysian’s participation in Bangkok transgender pageant
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) has strongly condemned the participation of an individual, allegedly representing Malaysia, in a transgender beauty pageant held in Bangkok last Sunday. “Religious authorities will work with the relevant agencies to examine possible action under existing laws,” he said. Earlier, a video showing an individual representing Malaysia at an international transgender beauty pageant went viral on social media, drawing mixed reactions from netizens.

items.title: ‘Baddestcoach’ defamation suit against Caprice heads to trial after settlement talks collapse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The defamation suit filed by renowned high-performance transformation coach Syed Mohammad Murad Syed Naseem, better known as Murad “Baddestcoach” Zaidi, against social media influencer Caprice will proceed to full trial following the failure of both parties to reach an amicable settlement at the High Court here. He added that the mediation proceedings, which took place on July 31 and lasted nearly four hours, were attended by both Caprice, whose real name is Ariz Ramli, and Murad Zaidi. On Nov 8 last year, the High Court recorded a consent order compelling Caprice to immediately remove and withdraw nine defamatory statements published on his Instagram account against Murad Zaidi.

items.title: Sarawak electoral boundary redelineation: 17 new seats proposed, 10 renamed
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 1 — Seventeen new state constituencies have been proposed across Sarawak under the Election Commission’s (EC) 2026 electoral boundary review, with Petra Jaya, Sibu, and Miri parliamentary constituencies each set to gain two new seats. Miri would also gain two new constituencies through the proposed Permaisuri and Tudan. In addition, the EC has proposed changes to the names of 10 state constituencies.

items.title: No changes to Perak Opposition seating despite Bersatu fallout, says Speaker
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 1 — The Perak State Assembly has not received any formal request to alter the Opposition’s seating arrangement following recent sackings and suspensions within Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu), Speaker Datuk Seri Mohammad Zahir Abdul Khalid said today. In June, Sungai Manik assemblyman Datuk Zainol Fadzi Paharudin announced his entry into Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan), four months after his expulsion from Bersatu. Zainol Fadzi was among 17 members sacked nationwide by Bersatu over alleged party sabotage.

items.title: Penang DVS: No clear offence under Animal Welfare Act for owner failing to stop dog fight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Animal Welfare Act 2015 contains no clear provision making it an offence for a dog owner to fail to intervene when dogs fight, the Penang Veterinary Services Department (DVS) has said. “There is no clear provision under the Act that (makes it) an offence by an owner for an animal fight or for failing to stop the fight,” DVS was quoted as saying. However, it said action could be considered under Section 8 of the Minor Offences Act 1955 if there was evidence that someone had encouraged or prompted an animal to attack, alarm or frighten another person or animal.

items.title: Merdeka break expected to bring RM36m to southern Thailand from 60,000 Malaysian tourists
items.summary: KOTA BARU, Sept 1 — About 60,000 Malaysians are expected to spend an estimated RM36 million in southern Thailand during the five-day Merdeka Day and school holiday period. The New Straits Times reported Thailand-Asean Halal Trade and Tourism Association president Aida Oujeh as saying the estimate covered travellers entering the country from August 29 to September 2. “The main destinations are Hat Yai, Phatthalung, Satun, Betong, Bangkok and Krabi.

items.title: Johari Ghani: US forced labour issue resolved, excess capacity still pending
items.summary: He said the investigation is close to being finalised, while Malaysia continues to engage with the US on the definition of excess capacity. “They have almost finalised the excess capacity investigation. Johari said Malaysia’s concern is that the US definition of excess capacity also takes into account capacity originating from third countries.

items.title: MOF: Budi95 and Budi Diesel monthly entitlements back to 300L today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The basic monthly eligibility limit under Budi Madani has been increased from 200 to 300 litres, effective today. The Ministry of Finance (MOF), in a Facebook post, said the adjustment covers Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) and Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel), with eligible recipients entitled to up to 300 litres monthly. The additional allocation raises the monthly entitlement for eligible private diesel pick-up truck and jeep owners from 300 to 400 litres from today.

items.title: Boy awarded RM359,123 after botched circumcision leaves permanent scarring
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — A Terengganu Sessions Court has reportedly awarded RM359,122.90 to a boy who suffered permanent scarring and extensive skin loss following a botched circumcision at a private clinic in 2023. The New Straits Times reported that Judge Wan Nor Aklima Wan Salleh awarded RM300,000 in general damages and RM59,122.90 in special and future damages after finding Klinik Perubatan Hijraa in Kuala Nerus medically negligent. The boy suffered serious genital injuries that required prolonged hospital treatment and further surgery, including full-thickness skin grafting.

items.title: Zahid Hamidi directs Rural Development Ministry to clear backlog by year-end
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Rural and Regional Development Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the move was important given that the time remaining until 2026 is not long, besides the cost of a problem would increase if decisions were further delayed. Ahmad Zahid said a comprehensive review should be carried out this month covering all projects, payments, land issues, utilities, contracts, assets and decisions that have not yet been resolved. “My principle is simple: No issue without an owner, no project without a timeline, no meeting without a decision,” he said.

items.title: NRD: MyKad printing services disrupted until Sept 7 for shift to new-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The National Registration Department (NRD) is transitioning from the existing MyKad structure to the new-generation MyKad, causing temporary disruptions to its printing services. In a statement today, the NRD announced that the printing disruption is expected to last from today through Sept 7. JPN also expressed its appreciation for the public’s patience and cooperation throughout this transitional period.
